_README: KNOWN-GOOD ACTIVITY SKELETON. Copy this whole folder into the activity's place in the tree, then edit config.json, marking.json and activity.html only. Never edit the shared engine for a content change. Question budget: Predict (structured, not scored) + Knowledge Check (3-4 auto items) + Explain + Apply (exactly 2 constructed). See CLAUDE.md sections 3, 5 and 10.
_assessment_security_note: REQUIRED READING (CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment). This file, config.json, is PUBLIC — it is what the student's browser fetches and can always be read, including before they start writing. It must NEVER contain markingScheme, accept, insufficient, dependsOn, rubric levels/source, or markingInstructions. All of that lives ONLY in the sibling file marking.json (see _template/marking.json), which the engine fetches lazily — never on page load, only when a teacher/marker PDF is actually generated. This is a client-side best-effort separation, not real security (marking.json is still a fetchable static file on GitHub Pages) — document it that way, never oversell it.
title: Activity Title
subtitle: One-line hook that makes a student want to start.
_assessmentMode_note: OPTIONAL, defaults to "formative" if omitted. "formative" (practice — the normal case) generates a single combined PDF exactly as before, just now built from config.json + marking.json together. "assessed" (graded work/tests) locks the attempt on Final Submit, gives the student only a submission receipt (no marking scheme), and puts the full marking PDF behind a separate ?teacher=1-gated action. See CLAUDE.md §5.
_learningFocus_note: REQUIRED. Prints as 'About this activity' on the evidence PDF and rides in the JSON, so leadership, parents and educators see the meaning of the activity. 'skills' is a short chip list drawn from the school's skill language (critical thinking, creativity, mathematical, digital literacy, communication, analytical, research, scientific enquiry...). 'summary' is ONE high-quality paragraph that names both the skills developed AND the specific curriculum content practised, tied to the course and module. Make it sound genuinely impressive and accurate — never generic.

learningFocus.summary: One high-quality paragraph naming the skills the student develops and the exact curriculum content they practise in this activity, tied to the named course and module, so a parent or head of department can see at a glance why it is meaningful.

orient.mission: A short mission statement in plain language — what the student is going to find out.
steps: Learn the key idea from the diagram.
Explain, apply, then answer the Knowledge Check.
Generate your Learning Evidence to hand in.
orient.realLife: Where the student meets this concept in their own everyday life.

predict.prompt: A structured prediction (multiple choice, multi-select or slider only — never prose).

investigate.title: The Interactive
investigate.lede: One or two sentences telling the student what to do and which variable is the control.

record.intro: Every trial is logged here automatically.
record.emptyText: No trials yet. Run one in the interactive.

_written_note: Student-facing only. maxMarks (a bare number) is fine to show — it doesn't reveal content. skillFocus is REQUIRED: a short, generic, non-answer-revealing statement of the broad skill assessed (e.g. 'Use evidence from your investigation and explain your reasoning clearly.'). NEVER put markingScheme, accept, insufficient or dependsOn here — those go in marking.json's matching 'explain'/'apply' entry.

explain.prompt: Ask the student to interpret a pattern they observed, using their own data.
explain.lede: Use the numbers from your Investigation Record.
explain.skillFocus: Use evidence from your own investigation and explain your reasoning clearly.

apply.prompt: Ask the student to apply the concept to a new, unfamiliar, real-life context.
apply.lede: Think about where this happens outside the lab.
apply.skillFocus: Apply what you found to a new situation and give clear, well-explained reasons.

knowledgeCheck.explain: Shown after checking: why the answer is right.

_rubric_note: Student-facing rubric: key/label/max/auto only, plus a REQUIRED 'studentHint' on every non-auto criterion — a short, GENERIC, non-content-revealing statement of what good work looks like (e.g. 'Use evidence clearly from your own investigation to support your answer.'), never the content-specific level descriptors. NEVER put 'levels' or 'source' here — those are marker-only and belong in marking.json's matching rubric.criteria entry (matched by 'key'). The auto criterion may keep a plain, non-revealing 'descriptor' (e.g. 'Knowledge Check correct.') since that doesn't disclose anything.

rubric.note: You are graded out of the total marks, shown as a percentage.

criteria.label: Use of evidence
criteria.studentHint: Use evidence clearly from your own investigation to support your answer.

criteria.label: Scientific reasoning
criteria.studentHint: Explain the scientific reasoning behind your answer, applying it correctly to the situation asked about.

criteria.label: Communication
criteria.studentHint: Write clearly, in full sentences, using correct scientific vocabulary.

_es_note: REQUIRED (see CLAUDE.md Section 15). Mirror every translatable field here in natural, age-appropriate Spanish, including skillFocus and studentHint. Arrays of objects with an 'id' (predict.options, knowledgeCheck) merge by id — keep the same ids, translate only 'label'/'prompt'/'explain'. Other arrays (orient.steps, record.columns, rubric.criteria, match 'pairs') merge by position. This file has NOTHING marker-only in it to begin with, so there is nothing to withhold from translation here — markingScheme/accept/insufficient/rubric-source/markingInstructions all live in the English-only marking.json instead, which has no 'es' block at all.
